federal_transit_administration_fta_formu.administering_agency: U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), Federal Transit Administration (FTA)
federal_transit_administration_fta_formu.description: The Urbanized Area Formula Grants program provides federal funding to local and regional government authorities for public transit capital investments, operating assistance, and transportation planning in urbanized areas (population 50,000+). Local governments play a central role as designated recipients or subrecipients, responsible for planning, implementing, and reporting on transit projects that address community mobility needs[4][2].
eligible_activities: Public transit capital investments (e.g., purchase and overhaul of buses, trains, and related equipment)[4].
Planning, engineering, and design of transit projects and technical transportation studies[4].
Construction and rehabilitation of transit facilities (e.g., maintenance facilities, passenger stations)[4].
Implementation of complete streets and active transportation projects that improve access to transit (e.g., sidewalks, bike lanes, ADA improvements)[4].
Mobility management and coordination programs (including non-emergency medical transportation and paratransit services)[4].
Workforce development and training activities for transit employees[4].
Crime prevention and security enhancements for transit systems[4].
resident_input_opportunities: Public hearings and comment periods: Local governments must hold public hearings or provide opportunities for public comment on major transit plans, service changes, and capital projects[4].
Community needs assessment: Transit agencies must conduct assessments to identify and prioritize community mobility needs, often as part of the transportation planning process[2][4].
Resident advisory committees: Many local governments establish citizen advisory boards or councils to provide ongoing input on transit planning and equity issues[4].

Annual planning/reporting with public input: The annual and long-range transportation plans (e.g., Transportation Improvement Program, TIP) require documented public participation, including outreach to underserved and minority populations[2][4].
federal_transit_administration_fta_formu.leverage_point: Participating in public hearings and comment periods on proposed transit projects, service changes, and funding allocations. Engaging with resident advisory committees or attending meetings of local transit boards or metropolitan planning organizations (MPOs).

transportation_alternatives_program_tap.administering_agency: U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), specifically the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA)
transportation_alternatives_program_tap.description: Provides federal funding for community-based projects that expand travel choices and enhance the transportation experience by improving the cultural, historic, aesthetic and environmental aspects of our transportation infrastructure. TAP funds support pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure, Safe Routes to School projects, recreational trails, and complete streets initiatives.
eligible_activities: Construction of pedestrian and bicycle facilities (sidewalks, bike lanes, multi-use paths)[4][5][7].
Safe Routes to School projects (infrastructure and non-infrastructure to improve safety and encourage walking/biking to school)[1][4][7].
Conversion of abandoned railroad corridors to trails (rail-trails)[4][7].
Community improvement activities (historic preservation, vegetation management, streetscaping)[1][4].
Access to public transportation enhancements (improving connections to transit stops, ADA accessibility)[4][7].
Complete streets planning and implementation (designing streets for all users, including pedestrians, cyclists, and transit riders)[2][4].
Projects that address transportation equity (targeting underserved or high-need communities, improving access for non-drivers)[2][7].
resident_input_opportunities: Public hearings or comment periods: Required as part of the project selection and planning process, often during the development of local Transportation Improvement Programs (TIPs) and Statewide TIPs (STIPs)[3][8].
Community needs assessment: Many states and MPOs require applicants to demonstrate community support and conduct needs assessments, often through surveys, workshops, or public meetings[3][8].
Resident advisory committees or councils: Some local governments establish advisory committees to review proposals and provide input on project priorities[3].
Annual planning or reporting with public input: The annual planning process for TIPs/STIPs and periodic program evaluations require opportunities for public comment and engagement[3][8].
transportation_alternatives_program_tap.leverage_point: Participate in public meetings and hearings held by local governments, MPOs, or state DOTs during project selection and planning. Submit comments during open comment periods for TIPs, STIPs, or specific TAP project proposals.

congestion_mitigation_air_quality_improv.program_name: Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality Improvement Program (CMAQ)
congestion_mitigation_air_quality_improv.administering_agency: U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), Federal Highway Administration (FHWA)
congestion_mitigation_air_quality_improv.description: Provides federal funding for transportation projects that reduce traffic congestion and improve air quality in areas that do not meet National Ambient Air Quality Standards (nonattainment areas) or that previously had poor air quality (maintenance areas). CMAQ supports a broad range of projects including transit improvements, traffic flow enhancements, alternative fuel infrastructure, and active transportation facilities.
eligible_activities: Public transit capital and operating improvements in nonattainment and maintenance areas
Traffic flow improvements including signal coordination, intersection improvements, and intelligent transportation systems
Alternative fuel vehicle and infrastructure programs including electric vehicle charging stations
Bicycle and pedestrian facilities that reduce motor vehicle emissions
Travel demand management programs and employer-based commute strategies
Freight and port-related emission reduction projects
Diesel engine retrofits and fleet replacement programs
resident_input_opportunities: Metropolitan Planning Organization (MPO) public meetings and hearings
Transportation Improvement Program (TIP) public comment periods
Air quality conformity analysis public review processes
Regional transportation plan development meetings
congestion_mitigation_air_quality_improv.leverage_point: Participate in MPO meetings and TIP public comment periods to advocate for CMAQ-eligible projects in your community. Engage with regional air quality planning processes to influence priorities for congestion reduction and emission mitigation projects.

surface_transportation_block_grant_progr.administering_agency: U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), Federal Highway Administration (FHWA)
surface_transportation_block_grant_progr.description: The most flexible federal highway program, providing funding for a wide range of surface transportation capital projects including highways, bridges, transit capital, pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure, and transportation planning. STBG replaced the former Surface Transportation Program (STP) under the FAST Act and provides states and localities with considerable discretion in project selection.
eligible_activities: Highway construction, reconstruction, rehabilitation, and restoration projects
Bridge projects including replacement, rehabilitation, and systematic preventive maintenance
Public transit capital improvements
Bicycle and pedestrian facilities
Highway and transit safety infrastructure improvements
Transportation planning and research activities
Environmental mitigation related to transportation projects
Intelligent transportation systems and advanced technology projects
resident_input_opportunities: Transportation Improvement Program (TIP) public meetings and comment periods
MPO long-range transportation plan development hearings
State Transportation Improvement Program (STIP) public review processes
Project-specific environmental review public comment opportunities
surface_transportation_block_grant_progr.leverage_point: Participate in TIP and long-range transportation plan public meetings at your MPO. Advocate for local priority projects during funding allocation decisions. Engage with state DOT and local governments on STBG-funded projects in your community.

enhanced_mobility_seniors_disabilities.program_name: Enhanced Mobility of Seniors and Individuals with Disabilities (Section 5310)
enhanced_mobility_seniors_disabilities.administering_agency: U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), Federal Transit Administration (FTA)
enhanced_mobility_seniors_disabilities.description: Provides formula funding to improve mobility for seniors and individuals with disabilities by supporting public transportation services and alternatives beyond traditional public transit. The program supports capital and operating expenses for transportation services planned, designed, and carried out to meet the special needs of seniors and individuals with disabilities.
eligible_activities: Capital purchases including accessible vehicles, wheelchair lifts, and mobility aids
Operating assistance for specialized transportation services
Mobility management and coordination programs
Volunteer driver programs and travel training
Paratransit service beyond ADA requirements
Projects that exceed ADA accessibility requirements
Contracted service with private providers
resident_input_opportunities: Coordinated public transit-human services transportation plan development meetings
State and local transportation planning process public hearings
Transit agency advisory committee meetings
Public input on project selection and funding priorities
enhanced_mobility_seniors_disabilities.leverage_point: Participate in coordinated human services transportation planning meetings. Join transit agency advisory committees focused on paratransit and specialized services. Advocate for expanded mobility options during public hearings on Section 5310 project selection.

raise_discretionary_grants.program_name: Rebuilding American Infrastructure with Sustainability and Equity (RAISE) Grants
raise_discretionary_grants.administering_agency: U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), Office of the Secretary
raise_discretionary_grants.description: Competitive discretionary grant program (formerly known as TIGER and BUILD grants) supporting surface transportation infrastructure projects that have significant local or regional impact. RAISE emphasizes projects that improve safety, accessibility, economic strength, state of good repair, partnership and innovation, and climate change/sustainability. The program specifically targets underserved communities and areas of persistent poverty.
eligible_activities: Highway, bridge, and road projects including complete streets
Public transit projects including bus rapid transit and rail
Passenger rail and freight rail projects
Port infrastructure improvements
Intermodal facility development
Bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure
Planning and project development activities
Resilience improvements and climate adaptation infrastructure
resident_input_opportunities: Pre-application community engagement and planning processes
Project development public meetings and environmental review
Local government grant application decision-making meetings
Post-award project implementation community input sessions
raise_discretionary_grants.leverage_point: Engage early in local discussions about potential RAISE grant applications. Provide community input and letters of support for projects addressing local transportation needs. Participate in project development meetings and environmental review processes for awarded projects.
